text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit rate on prod after the tokenizer vendor bumped the vocab mapping (not the model). Investigating correlation with token IDs shifting vs our keying.

zheng: ugh. which model/quant?

maria: r-instruct-3b-8q8 (quantized), but the same client prefixes on fp16 tests show less impact. hit rates: before 0.62 -> after 0.50 on the same 24h traffic sample. latency p95 up ~18ms.

alyssa: do we know if the system prompt gets re-serialized differently? whitespace or tool fields ordering can change the token split.

maria: good call. I diffed prefix->key generation for ~500k requests. Root cause looks like token id remapping causing different first N token IDs in the cache key. Our current key = hash(model_version + tokenizer_id + first_64_token_ids + tool_meta_json_compact). That "first_64_token_ids" is raw token ids concatenated.

sam: so tokenizer vendor changed vocab ids — that will break exact-match keying. We should avoid raw IDs in keys or pin tokenizer version in the client.

kai: maybe switch to a normalized text fingerprint instead of raw ids? e.g. normalize -> unicode NFC -> collapse spaces -> truncate -> hash. Cheaper to compute and stable across token id remaps if canonicalization is right. But might lose precision for subtle tokenization differences.

maria: prototype I ran: two keying approaches on same sample traffic (50k reqs):
- old_raw_ids: hit_rate=0.498, avg_key_build_ms=0.9
- text_fingerprint_nfc_trim: hit_rate=0.585, avg_key_build_ms=1.6
So fingerprint improves hit-rate but doubles key build CPU. Still net token savings were positive.

alyssa: can we hybridize? keep model+tok_version in key; allow fingerprint fallback when tok_version mismatch. That way pinned clients keep fast raw-id keys, but after vendor changes we still get decent reuse.

zheng: architecture note: any switch that inflates key compute time impacts tail latency if we do it on the hot path. Consider async warmup/probing to pre-populate. E.g. accept request -> immediate route to a cheap low-quality model variant while background worker computes fingerprint & warms KV for the real model.

sam: also flagging that tool/function call fields are noisy: ordering of argument names from the platform (we stringify map) causes key variance. We should canonicalize tool args: sort keys, drop empty defaults, and optionally hash blobs (attachments).

maria: proposed short-term mitigations:
1) pin tokenizer version in client rollout (announce to customers).
2) add tokenizer_id to key (we already do, but we must propagate vendor patch to runtime configs).
3) implement canonicalizer: NFC + collapse whitespace + remove zero-width chars + deterministic JSON sort for tool_meta.
4) enable text-fingerprint fallback when tok_version != runtime_tok_version for customer.

kai: long-term: make cache keying pluggable per-customer: raw-id (fast), normalized-text (robust), probed-fingerprint (adaptive). Also add a live "probe" sampler that takes 1% of requests and computes both keys to measure drift without impacting production routing.

alyssa: on warmup: current prefetch warms based on full-length prefix tokens. For short prefixes, warmed KV isn't very helpful because model kernels choose different kernels for longer seqs. We should warm by (prefix_hash, seq_bucket) where seq_bucket = ceil(prefix_len / 64). Helps kernel selection consistency.

maria: perf profiling notes I attached to the run:
```
# warmup_probe profile (span samples)
key_build_text_fingerprint: 1.6ms (median) 5.8ms (p95)
key_build_raw_ids: 0.9ms (median) 2.1ms (p95)
kv_lookup: 0.45ms (median) 1.8ms (p95)
kernel_select: 0.7ms (median) 3.2ms (p95)
end_to_end_delta_after_change: +18ms p95
```
Note p95 spike mainly from key_build p95.

zheng: maybe offload fingerprint hashing to worker thread / kernel-bound util on GPU? We can use a lightweight xxhash on normalized UTF-8, or better, memchr-based whitespace collapse to reduce CPU. Avoid allocations in hot path.

sam: Also see regressions where kv warmup misses because TTL eviction policy uses absolute insertion time; when we rebuild caches during canary deploys we should keep a grace window to avoid mass misses. Change suggestion: use sliding expiry for warmup entries or preserve prefix tombstones across rolling restarts.

infra-bot: deploy: rollout/bump-tokenizer-config to canary (10% hosts) queued by @maria

maria: testing plan I'm going to run:
- 24h A/B in prod canary (10%) comparing old vs hybrid keying (raw-id primary, fingerprint fallback).
- enable 1% dual-probe to collect both keys and compute divergence metrics.
- add seq_bucket warmup for canary hosts.
- telemetry: new metric prefix_cache_fallback_rate, key_build_ms histogram, probe_key_divergence.

kai: +1 for dual-probe metric. Also add a "tokenizer drift" alert when probe divergence > 5% over 1h.

alyssa: will put up a small PR for deterministic tool_meta serialization (sort + remove empties) and a microbenchmark.

zheng: I'll look into moving fingerprint to a cheap C extension we can call from the runtime and evaluate offload to a worker pool.

sam: can we also publish a short customer note about tokenizer pinning and explain why sudden hit rate drops can be caused by token ID remapping? helps reduce pager noise.

maria: thanks all. I'll open the canary rollout ticket and link dual-probe dashboards. If we observe >8% hit-rate improvement with hybrid, we ship fallback in the hot path.

kai: and follow-on: evaluate kernel selection sensitivity to short vs long warmups after we have stable hit rates. maybe we'll need per-kernel warmup heuristics.

maria: ending checklist: create canary ticket, PR for tool_meta canonicalizer, telemetry changes, dual-probe implementation, short customer comms. cc @alyssa @zheng @sam

sam: :thumbsup:
